summary: Intermittent egress routing loop during failover causing p99 latency spikes for enterprise customer
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated p99 latency spikes (up to 2.6s) for requests pinned to us-east. Spikes correlate with automatic region failovers observed during a capacity shuffle.

Impact: BrightHealth Analytics (enterprise) observed degraded request-level latency for production models (~5% of traffic) for ~3 hours during a maintenance window; business-critical pipelines delayed.

Environment: prod-us-east, Redwood hosted API, dedicated routing policy with regional affinity enabled.

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Send steady request stream to pinned endpoint (customer uses region pin TTL=30m).
2) Trigger a capacity rebalancing event (internal or simulated by failover stub).
3) Observe intermittent responses routed to eu-west and returned via a different egress path.
4) p99 latency increases and some streaming connections reset.

Observed logs / traces:
- Gateway logs show repeated 307-level route handoffs between us-east edge and eu-west serving nodes.
- Tracing spans show multiple DNS lookups for serving pool during a single request lifecycle.
- No application 5xx responses; timeouts and connection resets present at the streaming layer.

Customer note: "We expected strict regional affinity during our pinned window. After a failover, some tokens appear to loop across edges and come back, increasing latency."

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Affinity map race during autoscaler-driven pool changes caused some requests to consult outdated routing entries, producing a temporary multi-hop path.
Action: Reviewed control-plane logs around 2026-03-10T09:00-12:00.

Hypothesis 2: DNS TTL expiration coinciding with pool replacement led to intermediate edge choosing eu-west IP for previously pinned session.
Action: Correlated DNS query logs; several edges reported TTL=0 events at the same timestamp.
    Findings: Two separate subsystems contributed: (a) affinity map update lag of ~4-6s, (b) aggressive DNS record rotation for ephemeral serving pools. Combined, they allowed a short window where a request left us-east and returned via eu-west, adding network transit time and handshake overhead.

Dashboards & traces: Grafana dash (https://grafana.redwood.local/d/egress-latency), Traces: trace-7382, trace-7390, trace-7401. See Slack thread #support (https://slack.redwood.com/support/C09ABC3) for live notes.
Related runbooks: egress-routing-runbook (linked above). Similar prior ticket: SUP-31290 (regional-affinity-routing-behavior-during-capacity-surge).
resolution:
Workaround: For impacted customers we advised toggling strict_residency=true and reducing pin TTL to 5 minutes until backend fix rolled out; this prevents routing across regions during pool replacement.

Fix deployed: Engineering patched the routing service to atomically apply affinity map updates and added a short jitter to DNS rotation to avoid synchronized TTL=0 events. Patch merged (PR #1428) and canary deployed 2026-03-12.

Post-deploy verification: Monitoring shows p99 returned to baseline within 30 minutes for affected customer traffic; no further streaming resets observed.

Follow-ups / action items:
- Ops: Add a metric for simultaneous DNS-rotation events across edges (owner: Elena).
- Eng: Add unit/integration tests for atomic affinity map swaps (owner: Marco).
- Support: Schedule a post-incident review with BrightHealth Analytics and include a small credit for SLA impact.

Ticket status: In Progress (awaiting completion of follow-up tasks and customer confirmation).
